title: Mirror Reflection
summary: In a square room with mirrors on all walls, except for the southwest corner, there are receptors at corners 0, 1, and 2.
statement: In a square room with mirrors on all walls, except for the southwest corner, there are receptors at corners 0, 1, and 2. A laser ray starts from the southwest corner and first hits the east wall at a distance q from the 0th receptor. Given the wall length p and the distance q, determine which receptor the ray first encounters.
constraints: A laser starts at the southwest corner of a p-square room and rises q while crossing width p.
Return receptor 0 northwest, 1 northeast, or 2 southeast.
reference_solution:
def mirror_receptor(p, q):
 from math import gcd
 common=gcd(p,q);p//=common;q//=common
 if p%2==0:return 2
 return 1 if q%2 else 0

hints: Unfolding reflections turns the ray into a straight line; the first corner is governed by reduced p and q parity.
Divide p and q by their gcd and inspect odd/even parity.
Even reduced p gives receptor 2; otherwise odd q gives 1 and even q gives 0.
The least common horizontal/vertical travel counts determine which room boundaries are reached at the first corner.
editorial: The least common horizontal/vertical travel counts determine which room boundaries are reached at the first corner.

tests.explanation: After unfolding, the first corner reached corresponds to southeast receptor two.
The first common corner corresponds to northeast receptor one.
